nodes.label: Personal Projects
nodes.details: Independent projects built outside of work.

nodes.label: AutoML Platform
nodes.details: An SQS-driven platform serving 27 per-client relevancy models, each promoted through an automated champion/challenger gate: every new training run is scored against a held-out sample of real traffic and only replaces the live model if it clears a minimum F1 bar without regressing past a set tolerance. Models are versioned in MLflow and cached on disk by run ID, a daily scheduler retrains against freshly reviewed data with no per-client config to maintain, and the same serving path runs Keras, PyTorch, or XGBoost models interchangeably depending on which one a client's run was trained with.

nodes.label: Confidence-Gated Correction
nodes.details: Each model carries two independently tuned confidence thresholds: one gates its positive predictions to a target error rate, the other gates its negative predictions to a ≥98% recall floor, since silently discarding a real match is unrecoverable while a wrong positive still reaches a downstream reviewer. Anything that falls below its threshold routes to Gemini for a second opinion; reviewed rows are folded back into the next day's training run automatically. A per-client freeze flag lets serving skip AI review entirely once a model has proven stable enough to trust unsupervised.

nodes.label: FAISS-Backed RAG Pipeline
nodes.details: Retrieves the top candidate passages from a tender's supporting documents via an HNSW index over Sentence-Transformer embeddings, reranks them with a BGE cross-encoder, and hands only the highest-scoring chunks to the next stage — cutting how much of a document a human reviewer has to read to answer one specific question. Embedding and query stages route independently across GPU and CPU workers so a short interactive lookup never queues behind a bulk re-indexing job.

nodes.label: Document Extraction Service
nodes.details: Every extraction request is grouped into the largest batch of documents that fits inside a single Gemini call's token budget; requests under that budget complete in one call per feature group, larger ones are split and processed across multiple passes so a token-cap check never blocks the whole request outright. When a document needs cross-referencing beyond what fits in one prompt, or a Gemini call fails, the service falls back to a retrieval-based pass instead of returning nothing. Three prioritized worker pools keep a single urgent request from queuing behind a bulk batch.

nodes.label: MLOps Triage Agent
nodes.details: An on-call agent built around Qwen3-30B served locally via vLLM, wired to 18 MCP tools spanning logs, metrics, and deployment history so it can investigate a production incident the way an engineer would — pull the relevant dashboards, correlate the timing against recent deploys, and narrow down a likely root cause — then open a pull request with a proposed fix, gated behind human review before it merges.

nodes.label: LLM Cost Governance & Eval
nodes.details: A weekly job re-tags a sample of already-processed records with Gemini and checks the result against what's already stored, per feature, using whichever comparison fits that feature's shape — exact match for a single label, set-overlap for multi-label tags, an LLM judge for anything too unstructured for rule-based comparison — and reports the accuracy trend so drift surfaces before it becomes a support ticket. A Redis-backed counter alongside it tracks daily prediction and review volume per model, the basis for catching runaway inference spend before it shows up on a bill.

nodes.label: ML Classification Services
nodes.details: Sector tagging runs each tender through a cascade of specialty neural nets — separate models for civil, electrical, and consultancy sub-sectors — then reconciles their output with keyword rules and a targeted Gemini pass reserved for the highest-value tenders, where a wrong tag is costliest. News relevance and categorization follows the same shape at smaller scale: one Gemini call produces a summary, a second scores relevance and industry category, and every service in the group falls back to a Gemini call whenever its own model is unsure rather than returning nothing.

nodes.label: Redis Cache Rollover
nodes.details: Traced sustained Redis growth back to cache entries with no expiry policy, then rebuilt the rollover to expire and rotate old keys on a schedule instead of relying on default eviction — cutting daily memory growth by 2GB with no change visible to the services calling into the cache.

nodes.label: BidAssist Crawler & Parsing
nodes.details: A multi-module Spring Boot crawler: Selenium-driven modules handle sites that need real browser rendering, a shared HTTP client layer handles the rest, and a dedicated scheduling module rotates crawl jobs and outbound addresses so no single source sees a repeated crawl pattern from one origin. Downloaded documents feed a parsing pipeline that runs Tesseract OCR over scanned PDFs and structured parsing over CSV exports, with a separate module watching for crawl failures.

nodes.label: AI SOC & DevOps Orchestrator
nodes.details: A sequential pipeline of seven agents built on Google's Agent Development Kit: a perception stage discovers in-scope assets and checks system health in parallel, an analysis stage scores anomalies and runs targeted vulnerability checks in parallel, and a decision stage — a magistrate agent backed by a chain-of-thought reasoning sub-agent — produces a severity verdict and hands it to an enforcer agent for remediation. High-risk remediation actions require human confirmation before they run; every agent step and tool call is written to a structured audit trail, and a guardrails policy blocks dangerous shell commands and flags prompt-injection attempts before they ever reach a tool.

nodes.label: E-Commerce Microservices
nodes.details: A small REST microservices architecture split by domain — catalog, cart, and orders as independent services — built to practice the same service-boundary and inter-service communication patterns used in production microservices work.
